title: How Many Outfits? Counting Principle Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Diya has three shirts and four pants. How many different outfits can she make, without trying them all on? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 6, Permutations and Combinations) we learn the first rule of counting: the fundamental principle of counting.

You will count the outfits one by one, then watch a live tree diagram branch out to 12 tips, and to 24 when a pair of shoes is added. We read the NCERT statement (m ways, then n ways, gives m x n ways), see why we multiply and not add, compare AND with OR, and fill four boxes to make words from ROSE with and without repeats. Two pause-and-think questions, the exam trap about a zero in the first place, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:

2:55 Repeats allowed vs no repeats
3:28 Exam trap: zero in the first place
4:02 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:36 Recap and three questions to answer
